intent: AI concept mockups for PuckIQ, preserving its current palette

concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished AI-generated UI concept board for PuckIQ, an iPhone fantasy hockey coaching app. Direction 01: PIT WALL. Explore a fresh design, preserving the existing racing-inspired identity.
Composition: landscape 3:2 board with THREE large portrait iPhone screens side by side, aligned and entirely visible. Each screen is a flat front-on UI rectangle, thin rounded perimeter, roughly 390:844 proportions. No perspective, hardware frames, floating layers, or cropped screens. Neutral warm-paper board background. Small board heading "PUCKIQ / 01 PIT WALL" above the screens. Prioritize readable actual interface design, no ad slogans.
STRICT CURRENT PALETTE: warm paper #F2F0EC; white #FFFFFF; carbon black #15151E; raised charcoal #24242E; racing red #E10600; subtle warm gray #E9E6E0; secondary gray #5F5F6B. Green #079455 only for positive metrics; amber #E08A00 only for warnings. No new brand hues. Carbon-black hero modules over warm-paper surfaces; crisp white panels and restrained racing-red indicators.
Typography: premium native iOS sans-serif, condensed heavy italic scoreboard numbers and strong italic page titles, tight grids, fine technical labels, generous readable spacing. High contrast, clear hierarchy. Tiny subtle rink linework within black hero modules.
Screen 1 TONIGHT: small top brand PuckIQ, team switcher "Top Shelf", settings icon. Heading "TONIGHT" and date "TUE OCT 13". Compact black timing-dashboard hero showing "10" and "players play tonight"; beneath three cells "8 STARTERS", "2 BENCHED", "1 EMPTY". Integrated red countdown strip "FIRST LOCK" / "00:37". White coach action section "Before lock" with two distinct useful cards: "Start Jack Hughes" / "Higher value in your C slot"; "Fill one defense slot" / "One usable game left tonight". Red outlined host action "Open Yahoo". Compact live-style player rows below with simple tasteful headshots, player name, position, game time. Screen 2 WEEK: heading "WEEK", Oct 12–18. Hero big "41" / "games that count", lower stats "48 SCHEDULED" and "7 BENCHED". Visual seven-day bar summary that makes empty nights obvious. White compact schedule matrix with rows McDavid, Hughes, Makar, Kaprizov and weekday columns, small team opponent chips; off-night columns softly shaded. A white insight card "Wednesday has room" / "Stream a player who fits your empty slots". Screen 3 PICKUPS: heading "PICKUPS" with short subtitle "Value for your lineup". Segmented tabs "This week" / "Next week". Position chips "All" / "F" / "D" / "G". Black featured card for a fictional demo player "Alex Turner", "LW · NYR", green "+6.7" / "VALUE ADDED", schedule chips WED and SAT and "Fills 2 empty slots". Small understated availability caption "Estimated availability". Below two clean white candidate rows and red-accent add buttons.
Every screen uses the app's actual FIVE-tab bottom navigation: Tonight, Week, Pickups, League, Roster. Active tab has a tiny red top bar, black icon; inactive gray. Native safe areas and coherent status bars. All figures and players are illustrative concept data. Do not suggest automatic host-league changes or guaranteed goalie starters. Mature, restrained, production-plausible sports interface; no gradients, neon, excessive decoration, glassmorphism, watermarks, or photographic backgrounds.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Generate an original premium mobile UI concept board for PuckIQ, the personal fantasy hockey coach. Direction 02: COACH BRIEF. This direction must feel much more editorial, spacious, calm, and action-focused than a conventional stats dashboard while keeping the current brand colors and sporting typography.
Composition: landscape 3:2 board, THREE large fully visible portrait iPhone interfaces side by side. Flat front-facing rectangles with native rounded perimeter, no hardware render or perspective. Warm neutral paper board. Small title above screens "PUCKIQ / 02 COACH BRIEF". Each screen roughly 390:844 proportions. Every screen includes status bar, safe areas, and bottom navigation. Focus on usable interface detail with large clear text.
Strict current palette: warm paper #F2F0EC, white #FFFFFF, deep ink #15151E, racing red #E10600, raised warm gray #E9E6E0, secondary gray #5F5F6B. Green #079455 used sparingly for positive pickup numbers and small positive markers. No other brand accent. Typography native iOS sans-serif, strong italic titles and a few heavy italic numerals paired with quiet regular body text. Rounded white cards, 20–24pt inset spacing, delicate dividers, restrained borders, much less black surface area than the existing app. No gradients or effects.
Screen 1 Tonight: brand "PuckIQ", team "Top Shelf" and settings icon at top. Small date "TUE OCT 13". Large editorial headline "Ready for puck drop?" with the word "Ready" subtly sporting in tone. A thin racing-red progress/countdown band labeled "FIRST LOCK IN 37 MIN". White summary card with huge ink "8" / "starters tonight", two smaller summaries "2 on the bench" and "1 empty slot". A bold but simple coaching section "Your next move". Large white card with a tasteful circular small player photo, "Start Jack Hughes", short clear line "Your strongest fit for the open C slot", a discreet schedule "NJD vs WSH · 7:00 PM", and a red button "Review lineup". Beneath a small quiet card "One defense slot is empty" and a link "Find a pickup". A final charcoal strip "Make changes in Yahoo" with external link icon; no automatic sync claims.
Screen 2 Week: header "Your week, at a glance." Short date Oct 12–18. Huge ink "41" next to a small red slash, caption "games that count". A narrow small gray bar shows 41 usable games and 7 benched of 48 scheduled, aligned clear captions. Spacious white seven-day calendar band with circular counts or small vertical bars; Wednesday highlighted by a tiny red underline and "Room to stream". Below, three white insight cards separated by fine rules: "Wednesday" / "2 open slots"; "Friday" / "1 open slot"; "Saturday" / "Full lineup". Minimal player schedule list, two or three rows, readable opponent chips. One subtle black button "See full schedule".
Screen 3 Pickups: headline "Make your empty nights count." Tiny subtitle "Ranked for Top Shelf". Simple understated position chips "All", "F", "D", "G". Spacious white featured recommendation card "BEST FIT", tasteful small headshot of fictional demo player "Alex Turner", "LW · NYR", prominent green "+6.7" with label "value added". Two clear schedule tiles "WED" and "SAT", small label "Fills 2 empty slots". Compact disclaimer "Availability estimated". A clear red button "Review player". Two smaller white suggestions beneath with demo player names "Owen Brooks" and "Leo Martin", green "+5.1" and "+4.8", and small red outlined plus buttons. Keep labels short.
ALL three screens retain FIVE bottom tabs: Tonight, Week, Pickups, League, Roster. Active icon ink with subtle red top line; other icons gray. Avoid losing the mature sporting identity; keep strong black typography and tiny precise red rules. All data are illustrative. Never show betting odds, AI chat boxes, automatic host roster updates, guaranteed goalie starters, or new unsupported capability claims. No logos besides PuckIQ, no watermark, no unnecessary decoration, no photographic page background.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create an original high-fidelity mobile design exploration for PuckIQ, an iPhone fantasy hockey coaching app. Direction 03: RINK VIEW. Make this visually distinct: the hockey lineup and open-slot story become a spatial diagram, with athletic bold typography and concise coaching. Keep all current PuckIQ brand colors.
Composition: landscape 3:2 board with THREE large fully visible, flat front-on mobile screens arranged evenly side by side, each approx 390:844 proportions. No perspective, no 3D device hardware, no floating components, no screen crops. Small heading "PUCKIQ / 03 RINK VIEW" on warm paper outside the screens. Mature, legible, plausible iOS interfaces.
STRICT palette: warm off-white #F2F0EC, white #FFFFFF, carbon #15151E, raised charcoal #24242E, warm gray #E9E6E0, muted gray #5F5F6B, racing red #E10600. Green #079455 solely for beneficial metrics, amber #E08A00 solely for a bench warning. No new brand hues. Subtle rink outlines, technical thin rules, big heavy italic sporting numbers, condensed all-caps small labels, clean rounded white panels. No photographic page backgrounds, gradients, neon, or gloss.
Screen 1 TONIGHT: warm paper header with PuckIQ logo, team "Top Shelf", settings icon, compact title "TONIGHT" and "TUE OCT 13". Main carbon-black lineup card labeled "YOUR STARTERS" contains a clear top-down schematic hockey rink, shown with thin quiet white/gray linework. Five small player portrait nodes positioned neatly and spaced widely, with large legible short labels Hughes / Kaprizov / Tkachuk / Makar / McAvoy and position letters. Along the lower edge of the rink card, two small goalkeeper chips in a simple row, not more player nodes on top of the five. One additional empty position slot indicated by a red dashed circle labeled "OPEN D"; it must read as fantasy lineup visualization, not a live hockey tracking system. At the bottom of this black card show compact stats "8 STARTERS" and "2 BENCHED". Narrow racing-red countdown strip "FIRST LOCK · 37 MIN". Under it one broad white coach action "Fill your open D slot" / "Find a player who plays tonight" with small red forward arrow. Small horizontal bench tray labeled "BENCH" with two simple avatar/name cells and amber indicator. Keep content fully above tab bar.
Screen 2 WEEK: warm paper header "WEEK", Oct 12–18. Black horizontal scoreboard tile huge "41" / "GAMES THAT COUNT"; small right value "7 BENCHED". Below a white panel "Where your lineup has room" presents a clean vertical stack of seven day rows Mon through Sun. Each row has eight small outlined slot squares, filled carbon for usable starters and blank warm-white for empty slots; Wednesday shows two open outlined slots and Friday one. Wednesday highlighted by a small red left rule. Tiny coherent legend "Filled" / "Open". Under the day rows a concise white insight card "WEDNESDAY OPPORTUNITY" / "A pickup can fill 2 open slots", and red understated button "Find a fit". A compact bottom row with player portraits and schedule chips is optional if space allows. No excessive table text.
Screen 3 PICKUPS: warm paper header "PICKUPS", small subtitle "Find the right fit". Compact segmented switch "This week" / "Next week"; position filters All / F / D / G. Large charcoal feature panel "YOUR LINEUP NEEDS" with two clearly outlined slot chips "WED · D" and "FRI · D", and concise copy "Open nights, better value". Below a white featured player card with fictional demo player "Owen Brooks", "D · UTA", tasteful small circular portrait, green "+5.1" / "VALUE ADDED". A simple horizontal match diagram connects the player's "WED" and "FRI" schedule chips with the two open nights above, all readable and contained within card. Text "Fills both open nights" and small "Estimated availability". Red button "Review player". Two compact white alternative rows "Noah Hayes" / "+4.8" and "Ethan Clark" / "+4.2" with understated plus controls.
All screens share actual FIVE-tab bottom navigation: Tonight, Week, Pickups, League, Roster. Active icon carbon with small racing-red line, inactive gray. Include neat native status bars and safe areas. All examples are fictional concept data. Keep this a fantasy hockey lineup coach, avoid betting odds, live location tracking, AI chat, autonomous host-league changes, or any promise of goalie starts. No watermarks. The diagram must look understandable on a real phone and never replace the useful coaching action with decorative art.
